source: rpms-ux product-cycle personas and use cases

use_case_index.name: Prepare for the visit and triage
See the patient and write the note
Order labs and act on results
Give an after-visit summary and care plan
Pay for purchased and referred care

roles.surface: BPRM; the text screens for Patient Registration
responsibilities: keeps demographics, tribal enrollment and eligibility current
goals: no duplicate charts
eligibility right before the visit, so the visit can be billed
roles.context: at the window with the patient in front of them, under time pressure; the first person to touch every visit.

roles.surface: BPRM; the text screens for Patient Registration
responsibilities: corrects what the front desk cannot: chart numbers and dispositions, legal name changes on proof, deaths
goals: one chart per patient, and every correction to a chart's identity on record with who approved it
roles.context: off the window, a few times a day on request from the front desk; holds the registration manager key, which the front desk clerk does not.

roles.surface: BPRM; IHS Windows Scheduling; the text screens for Scheduling
responsibilities: manages clinic slots and the wait list
goals: fill the clinic's slots
the patient knows when and where to come
roles.context: on the phone or at the window; works across many clinics' schedules at once.

responsibilities: records the reason for the visit, allergies and screenings
goals: the provider walks into a room with the chart ready
roles.context: in the exam room, a few minutes per patient, on the chart the provider will use next.

roles.surface: VueCentric; BPRM for ward transfers and the census
responsibilities: follows up on results and messages
goals: the right patient sees the provider first
nothing ordered is lost
roles.context: between rooms and the phone; works the Notifications tab.

responsibilities: examines the patient, sets the purpose of visit, orders, prescribes, refers, writes and signs the note
goals: a signed note and a codeable visit by the end of the day, with as few clicks as possible
roles.context: the Cover Sheet to Notes path in VueCentric, in the room or right after.

roles.surface: VueCentric; the text screens for visit data entry
responsibilities: assigns or corrects E&M, CPT and ICD codes
goals: every visit coded correctly, and before the billing deadline
roles.context: works a queue of signed visits, a day or more after the visit.

roles.surface: The text screens for Third Party Billing and Accounts Receivable
responsibilities: reviews claims generated from coded visits
goals: clean claims to Medicare and Medicaid first time
denials worked
roles.context: the text screens for Third Party Billing and Accounts Receivable; never sees VueCentric.

roles.surface: VueCentric's Reports tab; the text screens for visit reports and the Clinical Reporting System
goals: numbers that match what happened in the clinic
roles.context: periodic, report-driven; reads output more than enters data.

roles.role: Care / case manager (nurse case manager, public health nurse)
responsibilities: keeps lists (panels) of the patients they manage, by provider, condition or criteria
works the flags on those patients (abnormal labs, ER visits, admissions)
tracks the care-management events each patient is due
goals: no patient on their list falls through: every flag worked, every due event done, every gap in the measures closed
roles.context: population-first, not visit-first; works across many patients at once, from a list, often between clinics and with a second case manager sharing the same list.

roles.surface: The text screens for user setup and Staff Credentials
responsibilities: sets up providers and staff as RPMS users with the right person class, keys, signature and credentials
goals: no provider sees patients before they are credentialed
no one keeps access after they leave
roles.context: occasional, high-stakes; the text screens only.

roles.surface: The text screens for Outpatient Pharmacy
responsibilities: verifies and dispenses prescriptions from provider orders
goals: safe, fast dispensing

responsibilities: accessions orders, collects specimens, files results
goals: results back on the chart quickly and to the right patient

roles.surface: The text screens for Purchased/Referred Care and referral tracking
responsibilities: tracks referrals out of the clinic
goals: referrals authorised within the rules and paid

roles.surface: BPRM; the text screens for admissions
goals: the record says who is in which bed right now
every stay has one admission and one discharge
roles.context: Holds an ADT key that allows moving a patient; a supervisor also maintains wards and beds.

roles.surface: BPRM; the text screens for incomplete charts
responsibilities: tracks each discharged chart's deficiencies by provider until the chart is complete
goals: no stay waits on a signature to be coded and billed
roles.context: Works a list of incomplete charts after discharge; holds the incomplete-chart key and cannot move patients.

roles.surface: BPRM; the text screens for Patient Registration
responsibilities: records every kind of coverage a patient has, the Medicare Secondary Payer survey and the order payers are billed in
helps uninsured patients apply, and tracks each application as a case
goals: every visit has a payer
no patient who could be covered is left uninsured
roles.context: Away from the window, by appointment or by referral from the front desk; works one patient's file in depth.

roles.role: Behavioral health provider (psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, counselor)
responsibilities: sees patients for behavioral health and substance use care
writes and signs the notes of those visits
goals: what the patient tells them is read only by the people the patient's care and the law allow (42 CFR Part 2 for substance use records)
roles.context: Works the same chart as the rest of the clinic, but their notes sit under titles whose business rules name only the behavioral health user classes; a user who is not in one sees that the note exists, not what it says.

roles.surface: The clinic, a printout, and the patient portal
goals: understands what happened and what to do next
can reach the clinic
roles.context: gets the after-visit summary on paper today.

groups.name: At the front desk
groups.blurb: Getting the patient in the door, on the schedule, and covered.

stories.text: As a front desk clerk, I want to search for a patient by name, date of birth, chart number or SSN, so that I don't register someone who already has a chart.
As a front desk clerk, I want to add a new patient with demographics, tribe and community, so that the patient has a chart and a health record number at this facility.
As a scheduler, I want to find an open slot in a clinic and book the patient into it, so that the patient has a time and the clinic's day is planned.
As a scheduler, I want to cancel or move an appointment with a reason, so that the slot is freed and the clinic knows why.
As a benefits coordinator, I want one list of everything a patient is covered by, with its dates and the order it is billed in, so that I can see what is missing or expired before the visit.

As a benefits coordinator, I want to record a patient's Medicare or Railroad Retirement entitlement, with each part's dates, and their Part D plan, so that Medicare is billed for the parts the patient has on the visit date.
As an admissions clerk, I want to admit a registered patient to a ward, so that the stay exists in RPMS and the ward knows the patient is theirs.
As a nurse on the ward, I want to record that a patient changed ward, bed, treating specialty or provider, so that the record says where the patient is and who is responsible for them.

groups.name: During the visit
groups.blurb: Seeing the patient, charting, ordering, and sending them home with a plan.

use_cases.name: Prepare for the visit and triage

stories.text: As a medical assistant, I want to sign on to the EHR with my access and verify codes, so that I work as myself, at my division, with my permissions.
As a nurse, I want to land on my notifications when I sign on, so that results, unsigned orders and messages are handled before new work.

use_cases.name: See the patient and write the note

stories.text: As a provider, I want the Cover Sheet to summarise the patient's problems, medications, allergies, recent vitals and appointments, so that I am oriented before I walk into the room.
As a provider, I want to select today's visit (or create one for a walk-in), so that everything I chart lands on the right encounter.
As a provider, I want to prescribe a medication that the pharmacy verifies and dispenses, so that the patient leaves with it.
As a pharmacist, I want to verify a pending outpatient order and dispense it, so that the patient gets the right drug with a label.

use_cases.name: Order labs and act on results

stories.text: As a provider, I want to order a lab test and be notified when it is resulted, so that I act on it.
As a lab technician, I want to accession an ordered test, collect the specimen and verify its result, so that the result reaches the ordering provider.
As a provider, I want to send a consult or referral and see its result, so that the loop is closed.
As a PRC clerk, I want to record a referral to an outside provider, so that it can be tracked and authorised for payment.

use_cases.name: Give an after-visit summary and care plan

stories.text: As a provider, I want to print a summary of today's visit (diagnoses, medications, orders, instructions, next appointment), so that the patient leaves knowing what to do.
As a nurse, I want to record the education given and the instructions for the patient, so that they appear on the summary and count toward measures.

groups.name: Between visits
groups.blurb: Staying in touch with patients and looking after a whole panel.

stories.text: As a nurse, I want to receive and answer patient messages from the portal, so that the patient reaches the clinic without a phone call.
As a patient, I want to send my clinic a message from the portal, so that I can ask a question without calling.
As a care manager, I want a panel of the patients scheduled today for two providers in my clinic, so that I can prepare for each of them before they arrive.
As a care manager, I want a panel of my patients whose latest measurement meets a criterion, so that I can offer them the service it calls for.

groups.name: Coding and paying for care
groups.blurb: Turning a visit into a clean claim, and paying for care bought outside.

stories.text: As a provider, I want to set the E&M level and confirm the POVs and procedures before I finish, so that the visit can be billed without a coder's rework.
As a coder, I want a queue of signed visits with their codes, and to correct a code with the provider's note in view, so that what is billed matches what was documented.
As a billing technician, I want every coded visit for a Medicare or Medicaid patient to appear as a claim, so that no billable visit is missed.
As a billing technician, I want to review a claim's errors and approve it, so that only clean claims go out.

use_cases.name: Pay for purchased and referred care

stories.text: As a PRC clerk, I want to decide a referral's PRC eligibility and issue a purchase order, so that outside care is paid within the rules.
As a PRC clerk, I want to issue a purchase order for an approved referral, so that the outside provider is paid.

groups.name: Running the clinic
groups.blurb: Credentialing staff, reporting on care, and protecting sensitive records.

stories.text: As a credentialing coordinator, I want to create a provider's RPMS user with person class, NPI, keys and an electronic signature, so that they can sign on, order and sign notes.
As a credentialing coordinator, I want to record each provider's licences, DEA and their expiry dates, so that I am warned before a credential lapses.
As a site manager, I want a count of visits by clinic and provider for a date range, so that I know the clinic's workload.
As a site manager, I want a list of visits with unsigned notes or no POV, so that they are finished before the billing deadline.
As a behavioral health provider, I want to write and sign my note under a behavioral health title, so that only the clinicians allowed to read it can read it.

As a provider who is not a behavioral health clinician, I want to see that the patient has a behavioral health note without being shown what it says, so that I know the patient is in behavioral health care, and their privacy holds.
